09_marg172: AFTER THE DEATH. The history of the book of Judges shows no small sacraments of mysteries. For after Josue the Judges succeed, as after Christ the apostles and the rulers of the Churches, to rule the faithful, whom he himself leads to the hope of the eternal promise. And throughout this volume are contained the sins of the Jewish people, and their servitude and their cry, and the compassion of God. For many years they served for their sins, and being converted they were set free; because our sins give strength to the enemies, and when we do evil in the sight of the Lord our adversaries, that is, the demons, are strengthened. But when we are converted, God raises up judges and saviours, that is, princes and doctors, whom he sends to the help of those who cry to God with their whole heart.
09_marg173: At the end of the book of Jesus Nave the narrator stretched the history briefly as far as [the time when] the children of Israel turned aside to worship strange gods. But in this book there is a return to the order [of events], how the things that followed were done after the death of Jesus Nave. The book, then, does not begin from that time when the people fell away to worship idols, but from the earlier times interposed, in which those things were done after which it came to these.

09_marg176: JUDA SHALL GO UP, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked whether some man was called Juda, or whether it called the tribe itself so, after its custom. But those who had asked the Lord were seeking a leader; whence it is thought that the name of one man was expressed. But because Scripture is not wont to name leaders when they are appointed without mentioning also the origin of their parents, and it is certain that after Jesus the people of Israel had leaders, of whom the first was Gothoniel the son of Cenez, it is rightly understood that by the name of Juda the tribe of Juda was signified. For the Lord willed the crushing of the Chanaanites to begin from it. And when the people asked about a leader, the answer of the Lord served for this, that they might know that God did not will war to be waged against the Chanaanites by the whole people. He said, then: Juda shall go up; and there follows: And Juda said to Simeon his brother: tribe, namely, to tribe. For the sons of Jacob, who were so called, were no longer living. It is manifest that the tribe of Juda asked for itself the help of another tribe, which it would return when there was need.
09_interl240: the tribe, namely, to the tribe
09_marg177: AND CALEB SAID: HE THAT SHALL SMITE. AUGUSTINE. Whoever shall smite the City of letters and take it, I will give him my daughter to wife. This is recorded in the book of Jesus. But whether it was done while Jesus was living and is now recapitulated, or after his death, after it was said, Juda shall go up, and Juda began to make war against the Chanaanites, in which war all these things are related as done, is rightly asked. But it is more credible that it was done after the death of Jesus, and was recorded then by prolepsis, that is, by anticipation, like other things. For now, when the deeds of the tribe of Juda against the Chanaanites are being set out, the order of the narration holds it thus among the other warlike deeds of Juda, of whom the Lord said after the death of Jesus: Juda shall go up; and after this the children of Juda went up to fight against the Chanaanite who dwelt in the hill country, the south and the plain; and Juda went to the Chanaanite dwelling in Chebron, and Chebron came out against him. Now the name of Chebron was Cariatharboc and Sepher; and he smote Sesi and Achiman and Tholmi, the sons of Enach; and they went up thence to the inhabitants of Dabir, whose name before was the City of letters; and Caleb said: Whoever shall smite the City of letters, etc. It is certain, then, from this order of events, that this was done after the death of Jesus. When, then, the cities given to Caleb himself were being recorded, the narrator, taking the occasion, anticipated what was done afterwards. Yet I do not think it is to no purpose that the Scripture has here recorded twice this of Caleb's daughter given as the victor's prize.
09_interl242: AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: The redemption of water: a land, namely, from whose fruits she might buy water, of which there was want in those regions to which she was being led as a bride.
09_interl243: AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: The redemption of the high and the redemption of the low streams; understand: which flow either in the hill country or in the plains.
09_marg178: NEITHER COULD HE DESTROY THE INHABITANTS, etc. In this very thing the Lord was with Juda. For God, being propitious, restrains even in the hearts of his saints the excess of too great prosperity, that he may turn the enemies to their use, not only when they are conquered but also when they are feared: the former to commend his bounty, the latter to repress their elation. For the enemy of the saints is the angel of Satan, who, the Apostle says, was given him to buffet him, lest he should be exalted by the greatness of the revelations.
09_interl244: AUGUSTINE. This was said in the book of Jesus because it was said while he was alive; but here it is recorded by recapitulation, since the Scripture was speaking of the tribe of Juda, from which Caleb was.
09_marg179: AUGUSTINE. Above it is read that the same city was taken and burned by Juda, and the Jebusites in it killed. But it must be known that two tribes, Juda and Benjamin, had this city in common, as the division of the lands which Jesus made shows. For it is Jebus, which is also Jerusalem. Therefore these two tribes remained with the temple of the Lord when the rest (except the tribe of Levi, which was priestly and did not receive lands in the division) separated themselves from the kingdom of Juda with Jeroboam. It must be known, then, that the city was taken and burned by Juda, those who had been found there being killed, but that not all the Jebusites were destroyed, either because they were outside the city or because they could flee; and that these Jebusites were admitted by the children of Benjamin, who had that city in common with Juda, to dwell in it together. What, then, is said: The children of Benjamin did not inherit the Jebusite, is to be understood that they could not, or would not, make them tributaries; or they did not inherit the Jebusite because they did not hold without him the land which they possessed.
09_marg180: AUGUSTINE. And Manasses did not inherit Bethsan, which is a city of the Scythians; it is said today to be called Scythopolis. Now it may perplex one how there can be a city of the Scythians in those parts, far divided from Scythia. But it may perplex one similarly how Alexander the Macedonian founded the city of Alexandria so far from Macedonia, which he did by waging war far and wide. So the Scythians too could have founded this one. For it is read in the history of the nations that the Scythians once held almost all Asia.
09_interl245: The Seventy: And Manasses did not inherit Bethsan, which is a city of the Scythians, nor its daughters, that is, the cities which it had established as their metropolis.
09_interl246: Almost the same is said in Jesus Nave, and in the same words. [unclear in the edition: "Ioannes"] Either it is said here by anacephalaeosis or it was said there by prolepsis, that is, either here by recapitulation or there by anticipation.
09_marg181: AND THE AMORRHITE STRAITENED. AUGUSTINE. And the Amorrhite afflicted the children of Dan in the mountain, for he did not let them come down into the valley, etc. This was recorded either in the book of Jesus Nave by anticipation, or here by recapitulation.
09_marg182: AUGUSTINE. And an angel of the Lord went up upon Clauthmon, the mountain. The writer called the place by this name because he wrote afterwards. For when the angel of the Lord went up upon it, it was not yet so called. For it took its name from weeping, which in Greek is called klauthmos. For there the people wept, when they had heard from the angel the words of the Lord punishing them because they had been disobedient, since they did not exterminate, according to his command, the peoples over whom they prevailed, choosing to make them tributaries rather than to destroy them, as the Lord had commanded. Whether they did this in contempt of God's command or from fear (lest the enemy should fight more fiercely against them to keep their life than not to give tribute), without doubt they sinned, either by despising the command of God or by not trusting that he who had commanded could help them. He would not say this to them through Jesus (if indeed he had already commanded that it be done while Jesus was still alive, and it was not rather recorded by anticipation, since it began to be done when he was dead) because here he willed to reproach all through the angel. But all had not yet done this while Jesus was alive, even if some perhaps had already begun. Yet it is more credible that nothing of the sort had begun while Jesus was alive, and that under him the children of Israel held as much land as sufficed them to settle in, although they had in their lots [the means] by which, increasing and growing strong, they might exterminate their adversaries. Accordingly after the death of Jesus, when they had prevailed, they chose to have tributaries according to their own will rather than to destroy them according to the will of God. Therefore an angel was sent to rebuke them. As for what is recorded in the book of Jesus, I think rather that it was anticipated: what was done after his death, or what he himself knew by the prophetic spirit would be, if the book which is called Jesus Nave was written by him; or, if by another, he knew that what he recorded there by anticipation had already been done after the death of Jesus.
09_marg183: AUGUSTINE. Hence we understand that certain sins come from the wrath of God. For that the gods of the nations, among whom, not exterminated, the Israelites chose to dwell, should be a scandal to them, that is, should make them stumble in their God and live having offended him, God threatened in indignation; which it is manifest is a great sin.
09_marg184: This is repeated by recapitulation. For the death of Jesus Nave too is recorded in this book, that all things may be briefly set forth as from the beginning, from the time the Lord gave them the land, and how they lived under the Judges, or what they suffered; and again it returns to the order of the Judges, from him who was appointed first.
09_interl249: Blessed is he who serves the Lord in the days of Jesus, who is enlightened by his word and wisdom, who is enlightened by his precepts and doctrine.
09_marg185: ADAMANTIUS. And the people served the Lord all the days of Jesus, and all the days of their elders, who were of longer days after Jesus. It must be known that each one brings it about for himself to be in good days or in evil, and to have the days of Jesus or of the just, or of the wicked. For if we understand "the true light which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world", and offer our souls to it to be enlightened, or if "the sun of justice" rise for us and enlighten the world of our soul, we have the days of Jesus Christ, the days of salvation. But if anyone has received the light that shall be put out, contrary to the truth, and has been enlightened by it, he will have days, but evil ones, and will not be in the days of Jesus, but in the days of Manasses or of Pharao or of any most wicked man. In fact, in the days of Acham [so the edition], a most wicked king, Isaias could not "see the Lord of hosts sitting upon a throne high"; but when the wicked king, whose days were evil, was dead, he saw by a vision of God. Now when the days of this or that man are spoken of in the Scriptures, the time of his life is not signified. Whence: "In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, till the moon be taken away." If we take it that in the days in which the Saviour abode on earth there were days of justice and peace, how shall we prove that days of justice and peace arose for those who crucified him and did not receive his coming? Or how was there abundance of peace in his days among those who delivered him to death on false charges? How did they have days of peace and justice in whose minds the darkness of iniquity and fury dwelt? And so, because those days are not now, justice does not spring up, nor the abundance of the peace of Christ, among the faithful [so the edition]. Rather, then, each one by the conduct of his life acquires for himself days of iniquity and war, or of justice and peace. Whence: "Unto you that fear my name the sun of justice shall arise", namely, to make for them days of justice, days of Jesus. But of the wicked it is said that "the sun of justice" sets for them, in whom, namely, justice sleeps and the darkness of iniquity arises. And elsewhere on the contrary: "Much peace have they that love thy law, and to them there is no stumbling block." The wicked too have their own light, from which evil days arise for them. Whence: "The light of the just is always, but the light of the wicked shall be put out." I do not know whether anyone would understand so foolishly as to think that there is some substantial light, one which is called the light of the wicked and another that of the just; which cannot be. For there is one light of the world, made by God, which shines on all in common and equally.
09_marg186: But it must be known that our soul is enlightened either by the true light, which is not put out, that is, Christ; or, if it has not this eternal light in itself, it is enlightened by a temporal one that can be put out, namely by him who "transformeth himself into an angel of light" and with a false health enlightens the heart of the sinner, so that the things that are perishing seem to him to be true goods. By this light they are enlightened who call pleasure the highest good, who seek riches, the honours of the world and earthly glory as if eternal. These, then, are in the days of his light, which is put out. For whatever they do or desire shall be put out. Enlightened by this light Marcion says that the God of the law is just but not good. There are, then, the days of Jesus, of which it is said: The people served the Lord all the days of Jesus. For he who has in himself the days of Jesus serves the Lord. For he cannot serve the devil or avarice. Nor can it be that he who is enlightened by the light of truth should serve falsehood. Let us pray, then, that Christ, who is the true light, may ever make good days in us, lest, the devil enlightening us, we ever have evil days, of which it is said: "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil." So too [there is] an evil world, according to the Apostle.
09_marg187: THEY SERVED THE LORD, etc. The people served the Lord all the days of Jesus. For it did not say that Jesus had one day, because his days are many: one day is justice, another sanctification, another prudence, another mercy, and the several goods of the virtues in which the Lord is served; and by these virtues of the soul the Lord is pleased. In all these days of Jesus thou shalt serve the Lord. Holy Scripture does not will that thou have some virtues and neglect others, but that, adorned with all these virtues and set in their acts, thou serve God. Similarly one has in himself the days of the elders, and serves God in their days, according to that: "Be ye followers of me, as I also am of Christ."
09_marg188: In the days, it says, of their elders, who knew all the works of the Lord, etc. He knows all the works of the Lord who does them; as the sons of Heli [are said to be] not knowing the Lord, not that they were ignorant, since they taught others, but because they acted as those who know not the Lord. Similarly it is said here: Who knew every work of the Lord. Not only, it says, did they know the work of the Lord, but it added every, that is, who knew the work of justice and of sanctification and of patience and of meekness and the like. Whatever comes from the commandments of God is called the work of the Lord. The contrary is the work of the devil: injustice, anger and the like. They know, then, the work of the Lord who do his work. Whence: He that keepeth the commandment shall know no evil thing, that is, he shall beware of it. Of Christ too it is said that he "knew no sin", that is, he did not do the work of sin. He knows, then, the works of the Lord who does them; he is ignorant of them who does not.
09_marg189: They knew, it says, the great works of the Lord which he did in Israel; as though some works of the Lord were small. I think that every work of the Lord is great; but according to the capacity of those in whom he works, if they are compared with one another, the works of the Lord are called great or small. For example: he brought the children of Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand, Egypt being scourged with heavenly prodigies. He made a way in the sea, gave manna in the desert, spoke to Moses from heaven, and gave the law on tables of stone. Are not these great works of God? But if thou compare with these that "God so loved the world as to give his only begotten Son", thou wilt find them small beside it.
09_marg190: AND OF THE ELDERS. ADAMANTIUS. The elders who were with Jesus or after Jesus are the apostles, who enlighten our hearts by their Scriptures or precepts, and make in us certain days from the true light of which they partook, coming into this world. He, then, who is enlightened by their precepts is said to serve God in the days of the elders who were after Jesus. And as Christ "was the true light which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world", so they were the light of the world, according to that: "You are the light of the world." They enlighten for us, then, days in which we may serve the Lord.
09_marg191: It belongs to God alone to know which among the elders after Jesus made a longer day, that is, who sent forth from himself a greater light: whether Paul or Peter, Paul, Bartholomew or John. Yet the saints are said to be of long days. And on the contrary, when the world shall be filled with scandals, "when iniquity shall abound, the charity of many shall grow cold": then the days to come are not called long but shortened, according to that: "Unless those days had been shortened, no flesh should be saved." The evil days, then, are said to be shortened, but the good days, in which we serve the Lord, long-lived and of much space. But "for the sake of the elect" the evil "days shall be shortened", the days of iniquity and scandal; and, as I think, once the evil days have begun to be shortened for the elect, they are ever shortened and lessened to nothing and at the last perish. Of these I think was one he who said: "Let the day perish wherein I was born." But the days of the holy elders are long-lived and lengthy.
09_interl252: the days of the saints are long; the days of the wicked are shortened
09_interl254: The Seventy: the great works of the Lord
09_interl255: the work, namely, of patience, of justice and of all the virtues
09_marg192: AND [JOSUE] DIED. In Paul Jesus lives, and in all who can say: "And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me", and: "To me to live is Christ, and to die is gain." In those he dies who, often repenting and sinning again, as it were insult the death of Jesus. Whence: "Crucifying again to themselves the Son of God, and making him a mockery." Not only, then, does he die in sinners, but he is also crucified and mocked. If thou thinkest of avarice, or of lewdness, if thou art driven by fury or by any vices whatever, Christ does not live in thee. Christ dies, then, to sinners, because in them justice, patience, truth and all those things which Christ is work nothing. But whatever works are done by the saints, it is Christ who works them. Whence: "I can do all things in him who strengtheneth me", Christ. Whence: He that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven; but he that shall deny me before men, I will also deny before my Father. Of those who confess he said that they confess in him, because Christ lives and works in them; but he does not say the same of those who deny. For he who denies is outside him; he who confesses is in him. It is said, then, that Jesus died, and there arose another generation which knew not Jesus, etc.
09_interl256: the generation of evil thoughts, which proceeds from the heart and makes one forget the great work of God; fearing which the Apostle says: "Be mindful that the Lord Jesus Christ is risen again from the dead."
09_interl257: Augustine expounds: how did it say, they knew not the Lord? In those glorious works, namely, which were done before them, that Israel might know the Lord.
09_interl258: that "he was crucified", namely, "for our sins, and rose again for our justification"
09_interl259: What each one loves and worships above all things, that is his god.
09_marg193: AND THEY SERVED BAALIM. ADAMANTIUS. And they served Baalim and forsook the Lord God of their fathers. These things indeed the ancients did; but because these things are written for our sakes, let us see that the things said of them be not said for the greater part of us. Hear the Apostle: Know you not what the Scripture saith of Elias, how he calleth on God against Israel? Lord, they have slain thy prophets, they have dug down thy altars, and I am left alone, and they seek my life. But what saith the divine answer to him? I have left me seven thousand men that have not bowed their knees to Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant saved according to the election of grace. Thou seest, then, that he interprets those who bowed the knee to Baalim and those who did not of the remnant of the believers and the multitude of the unbelievers. For those who were unbelieving in the time of the Saviour bowed the knee to Baalim, but not those who believed and fulfilled the works of faith. For it is nowhere read that in the time of the Saviour anyone bent the knee to idols. But this is said of those who are held fettered by sins. Whence it is certain that when we sin we bow our knees to Baalim; we who have been called to this, to bend the knee in the name of Jesus, and to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom all paternity in heaven and earth is named. But it profits nothing if we bend the knees of the body to God in prayer, and the knees of the heart to the devil. For if I do not stand firm against his wiles, I have bent my knees to the devil; and if I do not stand constantly against anger, I have bent my knees to anger. The same is to be thought of all the vices. So did they who worshipped Baalim and forsook the God of their fathers. What each one worships, admires and loves before the rest, that is his god. This is what God asks of man before all things and above all things: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, etc.; desiring in a manner to take up for himself all the affections of the human mind, and knowing that what one has loved with his whole heart and whole soul and all his strength, that is his god. What, then, each one loves above all things, that is his god. With very many the love of gold and of avarice outweighs, and he says to them: "You cannot serve God and mammon", that is, avarice. In others the love of pleasure, or of worldly glory, or of human dignity. Few are they in whom the love of God outweighs. Hence the error of all heathenism took its beginning, while men will have the things they greatly love to be gods, and ascribe the divine name to human vices and desires. For those greedy of money and burning with the love of avarice call Mammon, among the Syrians, the god of covetousness; the lovers of lust and pleasure ascribe to themselves Venus as the goddess of this vice by which they are driven. Similarly in the other vices they made for themselves a god of the very affection by which they are urged. Whence the Apostle: Covetousness, which is the service of idols. When, then, we love any vices with our whole heart, our whole soul and all our strength, we adore idols.
09_interl260: See how much sins do: God, in whom there is no affection of anger, no motion of passion, is said to be provoked to wrath; but he remains unchangeable. I, when I sin, take wrath upon myself; whence: "Thou treasurest up to thyself wrath against the day of wrath", etc.
09_marg194: AUGUSTINE. And they served Baal and the Astartes. Baal is said to be the name of Jupiter among those nations, and Astarte that of Juno. For the Punic people seem to call a lord Baal, and the lord of heaven Baalsamen; and without doubt they call Juno Astarte. And because these tongues differ little, the Scripture says here that they served Baal and the Astartes, that is, Jupiter and the Junos; nor did it say Astarte in the singular, but referred the sense to the multitude of the images. Yet I think that for the sake of variety it chose to mention Jupiter in the singular and Juno in the plural.
09_marg195: AND THE LORD BEING ANGRY, etc. ORIGEN. According to the Seventy: and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about. But in the Psalm it is said: "Thou hast sold thy people for no price", and in the Prophet: You were sold gratis, and you shall be redeemed without money. Why, then, sold, if gratis, and not rather given? Or perhaps it is a manner of speech of the Scriptures that one is said to be sold even when given. This sense is best there: You were sold gratis, and: "Thou hast sold thy people for no price"; because the wicked merited that the people be delivered to them not by worshipping God, so that the worship itself might seem the price. But as to what is said, and you shall be redeemed without money: it does not say without price, but without money, that the price of the redemption may be understood to be the blood of the immaculate Lamb. For by money the Prophet signified all wealth, because they were to be redeemed by the price of the blood of Christ, not by a price of money.
09_marg196: ORIGEN. When one serves God he is not delivered into the hands of plunderers; but when he forsakes God and serves his own passions, he is delivered up to shameful affections and "to a reprobate sense, to do those things which are not convenient", because he "is filled with all iniquity, wickedness, fornication" and the like. For if we sin against the Lord and worship our pleasures and desires as God, we are delivered into the hand of the devil by apostolic authority, as he himself says: "I have delivered such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved." Not only through angels does God deliver sinners into the hands of enemies, but also through the prelates of the Church, who have the power of loosing and binding. And they are delivered to the destruction of the flesh when for their sins they are separated from the body of Christ. And they are delivered in two ways: when, namely, the sin is manifest to the Church, and one is driven out of the Church by the priests, that, marked by men, he may blush, and, being converted, that may come about which follows, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord; or, when the sin is not manifest to men, but God, who seeth in secret, seeing his mind serving vices and passions, and that he is not worshipped in his heart, but avarice or lust or the like, himself delivers such a one to Satan. For he turns away and flees from his evil thoughts and unworthy desires, and leaves the house of his heart empty. Then the unclean spirit which had gone out of the man, finding his house empty and swept, takes with him seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and entering in they dwell there, and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. So it is to be understood that God delivers those whom he delivers, not because he himself delivers anyone, but he forsakes the unworthy and does not dwell in them. And the soul is said to be delivered from this, that it is found empty of God and is invaded by the wicked spirit. Let us watch, then, and purge ourselves of vices, that we may keep God within us, lest we be delivered to the devil.
09_interl261: AUGUSTINE. The cause is plain why Jesus did not destroy all those nations: that there might be, namely, those in whom these might be proved. And they could have been of profit, if, tried in them, they were not found reprobate, but were found such as the Lord commanded them to be. For the nations would be taken away if they lived so, nor would wars be necessary for them.
09_interl262: the words of the writer explaining why those nations were not destroyed
09_interl263: AUGUSTINE. Who were, namely, with Jesus while he lived; for when they were dead, another generation arose which began to offend the Lord, for the proving of whom the nations were not destroyed.
09_interl264: as though Jesus should not seem to have left those nations by human counsel
09_interl265: AUGUSTINE. This, then, was the cause, for their trial, that they might learn wars, that is, that they might make war with as great piety and obedience to the law of God as their fathers, who pleased God even in making war; not because war is desirable, but because piety is praiseworthy even in war.
09_interl266: AUGUSTINE. Satrapies are so called as it were small kingdoms over which satraps presided; which name in those parts is, or was, one of a certain honour.
09_interl267: AUGUSTINE. Not that God, the knower of all things, even of things to come, might know, but that they themselves might know, and by their own conscience might either glory or be convicted.
09_marg197: AUGUSTINE. In Deuteronomy God says of these nations: I will not cast them out in one year, lest the land be brought into a wilderness and the wild beasts multiply against thee. By little and little I will cast them out, until thou be increased and grow and inherit the land. He could have kept this promise of his toward the obedient, so that the extermination of those nations should take place as the Israelite portions grew, since their multitude would not suffer the lands from which the adversaries were exterminated to be deserted. But as to what he says, lest the wild beasts multiply against thee, it is a wonder if he did not mean bestial desires and lusts to be understood, which are wont to arise from a sudden success of earthly felicity. For God could not exterminate men and be unable [to exterminate] beasts.
09_interl268: because they treasured up wrath for themselves
09_marg198: ADAMANTIUS. And the Lord delivered them into the hands of Chusan Rasathaim king of Mesopotamia. Chusan Rasathaim is interpreted their humiliation. They were delivered to him, then, that he might humble them; and because they acted impiously on the heights of the mountains against the most High, they were delivered by him into humiliation. Nor did divine providence of old only deliver to be humbled those who were impiously exalted, that contraries might be cured by contraries with a wholesome medicine, but it does the same now too in its Church. There is now too a Chusan Rasathaim, king of Mesopotamia, to whom are delivered, to be humbled and afflicted, the souls which, despising Christian humility, have lifted themselves up into pride, which is very hateful in the sight of God. For pride is the beginning of departing from God; but "God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble." If anyone, then, despising the humility of Christ (who for our sakes, being God, was made man and humbled even unto death), is lifted up and leaps forward to the powers and dignities of the world, and does not shrink from the arts by which these are attained, even if they be against faith and religion, it comes about that he does evil in the sight of the Lord; and when he has obtained the highest insignia of power, and has climbed to the very summit of pride, thence cast down he is delivered to Chusan Rasathaim, namely to one of the princes of the air, as elsewhere to Pharao, and elsewhere to Chiram, that he may humble him who had been too much exalted, and afflict him until he come to his senses and seek the Lord, because while he was in pride he knew him not.
09_marg199: Anyone, even a little or least one, even if he has enjoyed no dignity, can labour under the vice of pride; and nothing is so foul, so execrable, as a poor man proud and a rich man lying. The disease of pride sometimes penetrates the very priestly and levitical order; and in us, who are set as an example of humility, and in the circle of the altar as on a watchtower for those who look on, the vice of arrogance stinks; and from the altar of the Lord, which ought to be fragrant with the sweetness of incense, the foulest odour of pride breathes forth.
09_interl270: as long, namely, as they served Baalim. For the affliction of penance ought to be according to the measure of the fault.
09_interl272: unless they had cried, a saviour would not have been raised up for them
09_interl273: "They cried to the Lord in their affliction, and he delivered them out of their distresses, and he brought them out of darkness", etc.
09_interl274: AUGUSTINE. Note that he calls a man a saviour, through whom God saves.
09_interl275: The Seventy: Gothoniel, which is: my time of God
09_interl276: some one, namely, of the archangels, sent to the help of those who receive the inheritance of salvation
09_interl277: hysterologia, namely a species of hyperbaton
09_marg200: See the kind Lord mingling mercy with severity, and weighing the measure of punishment with a just and clement balance. He does not deliver sinners up for ever; but as long, it says, as they served Baalim, so long do they serve Chusan Rasathaim, that is, eight years. Learn this, thou who knowest that thou hast erred: as long as thou hast sinned, so long humble thyself to God in the confession of penance. Do not wait for Chusan Rasathaim to humble thee and for necessity to wring penance from thee unwilling. Forestall the hands of the torturer, because if thou correct thyself, the Lord is kind, who will temper vengeance to him who forestalls it by repenting. And it is to be noted that while they served Chusan Rasathaim and did not cry to the Lord, no one was raised up who could save them. When, then, they cried, he raised up for them as saviour Gothoniel, who is interpreted my time of God, through whom that people was rescued from servitude, and peace was restored to the people, which pride and the various crimes of the people had put to flight.
09_marg201: And Gothoniel seems to me to be one of the heavenly host and the archangelic troops who are sent to the help of those who receive the inheritance of salvation. For there are saving angels, who are signified by Gothoniel or Aod.
09_interl278: it is shown of what family, of what nobility he is
09_interl279: of a wonderful man, namely, who was the companion of Josue
09_marg202: It is great praise of the first judge that the spirit of the Lord came upon him and that he judged the people by the Spirit of God; which I do not well remember to have been said of another. There are today judges of the churches, to whom is given even the judgment of souls. But I know not whether any is worthy "to be filled with the Spirit of God".
09_marg203: ADAMANTIUS. After, namely, they cried to the Lord. Who among us sends forth so strong, so just a cry to the Lord that the people may merit to receive a judge whom the Spirit of God may fill, so that he may hold right judgment? Whence the book itself is called of Judges, of those, namely, who judged the people of Israel: wonderful men, namely, as Josue was. So too the book of Kings, in which it is told how each of the kings reigned and what he did, even evil, that the princes or judges of the Church may imitate their good deeds and beware of their evil.
09_interl280: because the spirit of the Lord was in him
09_interl281: Great is the bounty of the divine clemency: for the sins of many they served eight years; for the justice of one they rested forty.
09_interl282: AUGUSTINE. As much time, namely, as the beginnings of the Roman empire had in peace, under Numa Pompilius only.
09_interl283: because, namely, the people was unworthy to have such a judge; whence follows: But the children of Israel did evil again, etc. Consider that, because they were unworthy to have such a prince, he is therefore taken from them.
09_interl284: Thou seest that our sins give and restore strength to the enemies, when we do evil in the sight of the Lord, and our adversaries are strengthened by the Lord. In spiritual things too the contrary powers would not grow strong against us, nor the devil himself, unless we gave him strength from our vices, and by sinning made him room to enter and to rule in us; whence: "Give not place to the devil."
09_interl285: most wicked enemies, to fight against Israel with him
09_marg204: ADAMANTIUS. After eighteen years the children of Israel cried again to the Lord, and he raised up for them a saviour, Aioth the son of Gera, the son of Jemini, a man ambidextrous. He who is raised up to save Israel has nothing left-handed in him, but both his hands right: a worthy prince of the people, a worthy judge of the Church, who does nothing left-handed, whose "left hand knoweth not what the right hand doth". On both sides he is right-handed: in faith, in acts; he has nothing of those who are placed on the left, to whom it shall be said: Depart from me, ye workers of iniquity, I know you not; go into everlasting fire, etc.
09_marg205: The divine Scripture almost marks the measures too: above, eight years; here it says eighteen. And it is certain that the times of chastisement are bounded according to the measure of the sin and the delay of conversion. For these eighteen years of servitude also passed, and it is not said that they cried to the Lord or were converted from their wickedness, but afterwards.
09_marg206: ADAMANTIUS. The saviours or judges who are raised up to set free the children of Israel signify the princes of the heavenly host, whom God sends forth to the aid of those who have cried to him with their whole heart and have bent the divine clemency toward them by the conversion of penance. For it is written that when our fathers had served Pharao a long time, they cried to the Lord, so that he himself said: The cry of the children of Israel is come up to me; and, sending Moses, he brought them out visibly. The destroying angel too was sent, who should lay waste all the firstborn of Egypt but touch none of the Israelites. And so it is plain that it was a heavenly power which, the Egyptians being laid waste, brought the children of Israel out of servitude. Under Sennacherib king of the Assyrians too an angel of the Lord is sent, who, having laid low a hundred and eighty-five thousand of the enemy in one night, set free both the city from the siege and the people from destruction. Similarly, then, when we sin, or are delivered into captivity for our sins, let us cry to the Lord not with the mouth but with the mind, so that the sorrow of the heart may bring forth a fountain of tears from the eyes; like him who said: "Every night I will wash my bed; I will water my couch with my tears." If we are so converted from evil things that we touch them no more, the Lord will send us his heavenly power, through which we may be set free from the devilish power; which may do all things for us right and prosperous, which may make us leave the left way that leads to perdition, and call us back to the right way, which says: "I am the way, the truth and the life."
09_interl287: having nothing left-handed, whose "left hand knew not what the right hand did"
09_marg207: WHO [USED] BOTH, etc. According to the spiritual understanding all the saints are called ambidextrous; the devil and his princes ambi-left-handed. For all that they do is left-handed and perverse, and assigned to the eternal fire with those who are on the left.
09_interl288: ADAMANTIUS. Whatever Aioth the ambidextrous does is right. He is right-handed with hands and feet. For he carries the sword on the right thigh, that he may come to the king of Moab and kill him.
09_interl289: "rolled, or a wheel-track". This is the discourse of the philosophy that judges pleasure the highest good
09_interl290: AUGUSTINE. He does not lie; for a deed is called a word, and he had a secret deed for the king.
09_marg208: ADAMANTIUS. Aioth is interpreted praise: for using a cunning art and a praiseworthy deception he slew Eglon, who is interpreted rolled or a wheel-track. The judges of our people ought to be such as was Aioth, who is interpreted praise, that they may cut away all rolling motions and the wheel-tracks of the evil way, and slay the king of the Madianites [so the edition], who is interpreted flux or outpouring. And who is the prince or leader of the flowing and dissolute nation but the discourse of that philosophy which judges pleasure the highest good? Him the evangelical and prophetic discourse kills, which is compared to a sword; which is shut up in their belly and inmost vitals by the disputations of the ambidextrous doctor, that, shutting them in with the assertion of the truth, he may put out every sense of perverse doctrine and gross understanding which lifts itself up against the spiritual knowledge of Christ; that every judge of the Church, doing this and fighting with the word of God, may become a praiseworthy Aioth, to whom the Lord may say: "Well done, good and faithful servant, because thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will place thee over many things."
09_interl291: because the Lord, who had raised him up as saviour for his people, had commanded him to do this
09_interl293: by disputing, namely, that he might put out every sense of perverse doctrine and gross understanding
09_marg209: AUGUSTINE. It is rightly asked how king Eglon was very slender, and the fat closed the wound when he was struck. But it is to be understood as said in that manner of speech by which things are wont to be understood by the contrary, as a grove [lucus] is so called because it least gives light, and to abound is said of what is not, and he blessed the king, that is, he cursed, as was said in the book of the Kingdoms of Naboth. For in that translation which is not according to the Seventy but from the Hebrew, we find thus: "Now Eglon was exceeding fat."
09_marg210: AUGUSTINE. How did the servants of king Eglon open with a key what Aod had not shut with a key? Or if he had shut it with a key, how had he not taken it with him, so that these could not open with a key? Accordingly either another key was brought, or the kind of fastening was such that it could be shut without a key but not opened without a key. For there are certain such, like those which are called [unclear in the edition: "verrudata"].
09_interl294: AUGUSTINE. Twice, namely, the time of the Romans under king Pompilius, which was memorable
09_marg211: AFTER HIM WAS. ADAMANTIUS. The Seventy: Semegar, that is, a stranger there. For all men of God are strangers in this world, like him who said: I am a sojourner with thee in the land, and a stranger, as all my fathers were. This Semegar, then, the Holy Ghost calls a sojourner there, that is, here. For what is there to the Holy Ghost, who is in heaven, is here to us.
09_marg212: AFTER HIM WAS, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked how after Aod Samgar fought for Israel and is said to have saved it. For it had not been taken captive or bound by the yoke of servitude. But he saved it thus: not because the enemy had done harm, but lest he should be allowed to do harm; who, it is to be believed, had begun to make trial by war and was repulsed by this man's victory.
09_interl295: The number six, which multiplied reaches six hundred, signifies the world finished in six days. He, then, is said to have struck six hundred with the plough, to whom the world is crucified through the cross of Christ.
09_marg213: WHO SLEW. ADAMANTIUS. Semegar smote the Allophyli, six hundred men, with the plough-handle, or the foot of the plough. I see another kind of praise in Semegar. He fights with a plough; Aod, it says, with a sword; yet he too conquers and lays low the Allophyli. It can be, then, that the judge of the Church does not always bring forth the sword, that is, does not always use the severity of the word and the sharpness of correction, but imitates the husbandman, as it were furrowing the earth of our soul with a plough, and often breaking it up with clement admonition, to fit it to receive the seeds. The Allophyli are slain thus too, when we do not use arguments and sharpness against adversaries, but drive vices and sins out of the minds of the hearers by a rustic and simple admonition.
09_marg214: Thou too, be the husbandman of thy soul. Use the plough which Semegar uses. But when thou hast put thy hand to the plough, look not back; that is, after thou hast taken up thy cross and followed Christ, after thou hast renounced the world and the things that are in the world, seek not again the things which for Christ thou hast counted as dung. For if thou hast thy hand ever on this plough, so that thou say confidently: "But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ", etc., a thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand, etc., but they shall not come nigh thee.
09_marg215: AND THE CHILDREN [OF ISRAEL] AGAIN, etc. As though for the sins of the people the good leader died; for the man of God is taken away from sinners and the unworthy. But someone says: When is the Church of God without a judge? If the former departs, another is brought in; [but] not always the prince of the people. The judge of the Church is given by the decision of God, but as our merits demand. If our acts are evil and we work evil in the sight of the Lord, princes are given us according to our heart. Whence: They have made a king, but not by me, and a prince, and not by my counsel. This seems said of Saul, whom the Lord himself had chosen and had commanded to be made king. But because he had been chosen not according to the will of God, but according to the desert of the sinful people, he denies that he was appointed by his will or counsel. So in the Church a ruler powerful either in word or in work is granted by God according to the merits of the people; or, if the people do evil in the sight of the Lord, such a judge of the Church is given, under whom the people suffer a famine and thirst of the word of God: not a famine of bread nor a thirst of water, but of hearing the word of God. Let us so act and pray, then, that we be not condemned by the indignation of God to this famine and thirst, that he be not taken from us who instructs us in the word of God and in work. For if we do evil in the sight of the Lord, Aod will die for us, and Semegar will be taken away, and our praise will be darkened, and we shall be delivered into the hands of Jabin king of Chanaan, who is interpreted sense or prudence. If, then, we do not like to have God in our knowledge, God will deliver us up to a reprobate sense, filled with iniquity, wickedness, fornication, avarice, etc. Thou seest who they are and of what sort, who are delivered up to a reprobate sense and to Jabin, the prince of the Chanaanites.
09_interl296: sense or prudence; for those who do not like to have God in their knowledge are delivered up to a reprobate sense.
09_marg216: ADAMANTIUS. The prince of the host of Jabin was Sisara, who is interpreted the sight of a horse. For he is animal, not spiritual, and sees nothing but the things that are animal. This is his sight. For he is ever looking on [them], and therefore the animal man, who is according to the flesh, ever persecutes him who is according to the spirit, until the animal man understands and examines all things, and understands whence help is to be asked for him, and cries to the Lord; until for that soul which has cried to the Lord prophecy is raised up, which Debbora signifies, and according to the grace and understanding of prophecy either the people of the Church is governed, or the sense of each soul.
09_interl297: that is, the sight of a horse
09_interl298: ADAMANTIUS. Observe that the children of Israel know not how to cry to the Lord unless they are delivered into the hands of Jabin king of Chanaan, or afflicted by Sisara the prince of his host.
09_interl299: by which a stiff-necked people might be afflicted
09_interl300: this is read of none of the judges
09_marg217: AND THERE WAS. ADAMANTIUS. According to the Apostle: All Scripture inspired of God is profitable to teach, to reprove, to instruct in justice. It is asked, then, what of doctrine or reproof or discipline this Scripture has, which is inspired of God. For what does it profit if we read that Debbora, a woman, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, judged Israel, etc.? First, then, this very thing, that while there were very many judges in Israel, it is said of none that he was a prophet, as it is of Debbora a woman, gives in this a consolation to the female sex, that it may not despair for its weakness of being able to receive prophecy, but may believe that it is purity of mind, not difference of sex, that confers this grace.
09_marg218: A bee, or speech; which signifies prophecy, which composes the sweet combs of heavenly doctrine and the sweet honey of the divine word. Whence: How sweet are thy words to my palate, more than honey to my mouth. And elsewhere the prophet says that the judgments of the Lord are precious above gold and much precious stone, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.
09_interl301: because the just shall flourish like the palm tree; whom prophecy, by instructing, brings forth to the palm of the heavenly calling
09_marg219: AND SHE SAT UNDER A PALM TREE. ADAMANTIUS. See in what places prophecy sits: between the heights, namely, and the house of God. Nothing lowly or mean can be found about the seat of prophecy; as Solomon says that it stands at the high gates of the cities, or dwells on the battlements of the walls, or moves freely in the high towers. It is said, then, to dwell between the house of God and the heights. For it does not teach us to seek the things that are upon the earth, but those that are in heaven, where Christ is, sitting at the right hand of God. Thither it exhorts us to go up; thither prophecy labours to move its disciples.
09_interl306: that is, a flash of lightning, which, namely, has a light that does not abide, for it quickly ends. This is the former people, which first of all was called by prophecy, through the prophets, to hear the words of God and to receive the gifts of the law; which shone indeed with the splendour of the law, but did not abide nor keep a continual brightness of light.
09_interl312: it shows that the palm of the first victory was not with that people
09_marg220: IF THOU WILT COME. AUGUSTINE. What is it that Barac, answering Debbora, says: If thou wilt go with me, I will go, and if thou wilt not go with me, I will not go; for I know not the day in which the Lord prospereth the angel with me? As if he could not hear the day from the prophetess?
09_marg221: ADAMANTIUS. I will not go up unless thou go up with me. Thou seest how prophecy brought the words of God to those former ones, and tells them that precepts are given them, to go up into the mountain; but they excuse themselves and say: I will not go up unless thou go up with me. And of the excuse indeed it is true, of the promise false. For they do not go up into the mountain of the Lord. But that they promise to go up with prophecy is false. For they did not follow prophecy so as to believe in Christ, of whom all prophecy is. Debbora therefore says to him: I will go with thee, but the primacy shall not be thine at this time. The Lord will deliver Sisara into the hand of a woman, etc. It shows openly that the primacy was not with that people, nor the palm of victory, but Sisara is delivered into the hand of a woman whose name is Jahel.
09_interl314: AUGUSTINE. See how the Scripture shows that God acts in the hearts of men to give to things the issue he has appointed. For he terrified Sisara, that he might deliver him up.
09_interl316: who before had had a covenant of friendship with him
09_marg222: AND JAHEL WENT FORTH. ADAMANTIUS. Jahel, a foreign woman, signifies the Church, which is gathered from the foreign nations. For Jahel is interpreted ascent, because there is no other ascent to heaven but through the Church of the manifold wisdom of God. She, then, while she ascends from bodily things to spiritual and from earthly to heavenly, kills Sisara, who bears the figure of the carnal vices and of the animal man. For Sisara is interpreted the sight of a horse, of which it is said: Do not become like the horse and the mule, who have no understanding. With a stake, then, she kills him, that is, with the point and power of the wood of the cross; and well is she said to have pierced his jaws with the stake. For the mouth which spoke of carnal things, and the doctrine which set forth the glory of the flesh, which persuaded the wise of the world that they should live in delights and pleasure, and had deceived by the flattery of luxury, is pierced through by the wood of the cross; because the way of pleasure which philosophy had preached as broad and spacious, Christ has shown to us as the strait and narrow way of salvation. So, then, Jahel, that is, the Church, delivered to eternal sleep Sisara, the prince of the vices, covered with skins, that is, lulled by the mortification of the members.
09_interl318: of moral doctrine, which befits little ones
09_marg223: GIVE ME, I BESEECH THEE. ADAMANTIUS. Sisara asked for water, but Jahel gave milk. The food of milk is called in holy Scripture the doctrine which is delivered to beginners as to little ones. For the deep and more secret sacraments are not to be delivered at once to disciples, but the correction of morals, the amendment of discipline, the first elements of a religious conversation and of simple faith. This is the milk of the Church; these are the first elements of the little beginners. But this food gives life and salvation to those who tend to the good; but to those who are pleased with contrary things, to whom luxury, lust, avarice and all impiety are dear, death. By the same foods, then, the good are nourished and the wicked choked; and where there is life for the pious, there is death for the impious; as wine helps the healthy, and gladdens the heart of man, of the healthy man only, but brings ruin to the fevered. So it is to be understood that Sisara, the animal man and prince of the vices, was killed by the doctrine of the Church, which he did not receive in faith.
09_marg224: SHE OPENED A BOTTLE. ADAMANTIUS. Let each soul lull and kill Sisara in itself with this evangelical and apostolic milk. For if anyone, taught by this, has mortified his members which are upon the earth, avarice, fornication and the like, he will be seen to have slain Sisara in himself; so that each may show these things to be fulfilled not only in the person of the Church but also in his own soul. Because, then, the former people began to pursue Sisara, but he was slain by a woman, that is, the Church of the Gentiles, and the palm of victory was given into her hand, at the consummation of all things, that is, at the end of the world, a canticle also will be sung to the Lord by Debbora, in which the primacy will be given to Jahel, that is, to the Church of the Gentiles; yet the praise of Debbora will not be silent, but one prize of victory will be given to the first and to the last.
09_interl320: The Seventy: a palm, that is, the wood of the cross, by whose point and power the Church killed the devil; which Barac, that is, the former people, could not do by the precepts of the law.
09_interl322: who had first begun to pursue
09_interl323: the Church from the Gentiles, which, as he passed by, had snatched the victory before him
09_interl324: Note that it does not follow, when Scripture says that a man went in to some woman, that he had intercourse with her, though it is wont so to speak; here, then, went in to her is said properly, that is, into her house.
09_marg225: AND JAHEL WENT OUT TO MEET. ADAMANTIUS. Jahel, that is, the Church, goes to meet the former people as it pursues Sisara. For Israel followed after the law of justice, but did not come unto the law of justice. The Church, then, goes to meet him too, showing him its work and the victory accomplished, and invites him into the fellowship of the overthrown enemy; because when the fulness of the Gentiles shall have come in, then all Israel shall be saved. The primacy, then, is in the hand of a foreign woman; yet Barac too is not shut out from the fellowship of the glory, who indeed began first but came last to the faith. Nay, while he is coming, the foreign Jahel in a manner snatches the victory from him as he passes. The same pattern went before in Esau and Jacob. For while Esau followed the things of the field and lingered in the woodlands, Jacob, coming before him and offering his father the food prepared by the counsel of the woman his mother, received the blessing of the primacy. In the Gospel too, while the Lord was going to raise the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue, the woman with the issue of blood, coming before, by her faithful touch first obtains health.
09_interl326: who had foretold in song that Sisara would be overcome
09_interl327: the husband of Debbora, who is also given as Lapidoth. Lapidoth is interpreted flash, Barac thunderbolt; because before he avenged Israel he shone among the people like a flash, namely by his merits and the prerogative of his works; but after he avenged Israel he was called thunderbolt, that is, smiting.
09_marg226: AND DEBBORA SUNG. ADAMANTIUS. If we remember what was said above, what Debbora signifies, what Barac, what Jahel too, who alone cast down the adversary, or what Sisara, who was laid low by the foreign woman with the power of the wood, we understand that all these are sacraments which are to be consummated through the Church in the last times, and that in this canticle there is described as it were an epinikion, that is, a praise, of the victory, namely, of that time when the last enemy, death, shall be destroyed. For then Debbora will exult, that is, the glory of prophecy will be made illustrious, because the things it foretold will be fulfilled; then Jahel, that is, the Church, will overcome the common enemy of all; and when the fulness of the Gentiles shall have come in, Barac, that is, the remnant of Israel, will be saved and received into the fellowship of the victory. Then, if we are worthy, we shall sing this canticle filled with mystical and prophetic sacraments.
09_marg227: THE SAME. In the beginning of the princes in Israel, in the willingness of the people, bless ye the Lord, etc. The blessing, it says, with which we bless the Lord takes place at the beginning [from] the princes in Israel, then in the willingness of the people. For example: when we first come to the worship of God and receive the beginning of heavenly doctrine, these beginnings are to be taken from the princes of Israel; and by the princes of Israel, that is, of the Christian people, I think the angels are to be understood, of whom it is said: Their angels always see the face of the Father who is in heaven. For example: if a boy goes to school, he is received by the master as a pupil, but he does not at once take the beginning of learning from the master himself; but when he has received from him only the first elements, he is handed over to others to be taught, as it were to the princes of that school, so that when he has been taught by them as far as is in them, he may at last receive the more perfect precepts of the teacher himself. Recalling, then, the beginnings of our instruction, prophecy says that when the princes have begun to work in us from the beginning, we then follow on with will and purpose, and, increased by progress, come at last to bless God himself. In the beginning, it says, of the princes in Israel. It is the beginnings that are said to be helped by the princes. After this we must strive with our own will and purpose, that we may merit to bless the Lord. For when the people of Israel was beginning to go out of Egypt and to cross the Red Sea, nothing was done by its own labour, but all through the princes, that is, through the angels. Whence: You shall hold your peace, and the Lord will fight for you. The destroying angel fought for them, who killed the firstborn of the Egyptians; of the Israelites he did not make even a beast to mutter. But we must not always wait for the angels to fight for us; only in the beginning are we helped by these princes; but in the course of time we ourselves too must go out armed to the battle. For before we learn wars, before we think of fighting the battles of the Lord, we are upheld by the angel princes; before we obtain the provision of the heavenly bread and are filled with the flesh of the immaculate Lamb, before we are inebriated with the blood of the true vine that came up from the root of David, while we are little ones and are fed with milk, so as to hold the word of the beginnings of Christ, we live as little ones under the angels as guardians and stewards. But afterwards it is said to us: Put you on the armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil. The Apostle does not suffer us any longer to lie hidden under the wings of those who give suck; he invites us to the fields of the contests. Thou seest how all things are done in order in the people of God: in the beginning the princes help. When thou hast been helped by them and taught, now do of thine own accord the things thou hast learned from the princes. For rightly, when the first things are digested and the rudiments laid aside, it is committed to our will, that either the praise may be deservedly ours, as sought by our own virtue, or the blame which comes through our sloth.
09_interl329: he calls kings those whom he calls together to hear the word of God
09_marg228: HEAR, O YE KINGS. ADAMANTIUS. Give ear, all ye satraps. As the satraps are inferior to the kings, so too to give ear seems to be inferior to hearing. For to hear belongs to the inner man; whence: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. But to give ear belongs to the outer and bodily hearing. Therefore those who ought to hear are called kings; but those who [ought] to give ear, satraps.
09_marg229: ADAMANTIUS. Exult, people of God; hear the marks of thy nobility. Thou art called to hear the word of God not as a commoner but as a king. For thou art a royal and priestly race; whence Christ your King is called "King of kings and Lord of lords". But if thou exultest in the title of nobility, learn by doing what each one becomes a king. Thou makest thyself king of all if Christ reigns in thee. For a king [rex] is so called from ruling [regendo]. If, then, the mind reigns in thee and the body obeys, if thou keepest down the vices with the bridle of sobriety, thou art deservedly called a king, because thou rulest rightly; and, made such, thou wilt worthily be called as a king to hear the divine words.
09_interl332: ADAMANTIUS. That is the voice of the just man, of tuneful voice and sincere mind, so that his song delights the divine hearing: who has in himself no hoarse sound of sin at all, and nothing of offence in his tongue, nothing of grossness in his spirit.

Whence: I count all things that are in the world as dung, that I may gain Christ, who has prepared all those things which eye hath not seen nor ear heard.

09_interl349: ADAMANTIUS. The bodies, namely, made subject to the soul, shining with the splendour of chastity and modesty
09_marg233: YOU THAT RIDE UPON FAIR [ASSES]. ADAMANTIUS. Ye mighty of the people, bless the Lord, you that mount upon the beasts, etc. Our body is a beast: for it is given to the soul for a beast and for service. It is said to the inner man. He who mounts upon the beast, that is, his body, and is made superior to the bodily desires, and has governed the motions of the body with the bridle of reason, [is called] to bless the Lord.

09_interl355: ADAMANTIUS. The sacrifice acceptable to God, which is offered in justice and equity.
09_marg234: As if: although God is to be praised always and everywhere, is he not rather to be praised and blessed here, who overthrew our enemies, as the Egyptians in the Red Sea?
09_marg235: ADAMANTIUS. The Seventy: The just were strengthened in Israel. In other nations those who are stronger in bodily might are called mighty in battle; but in Israel those who are more just, because justice, even when weak in strength, conquers; but injustice, even if it has many strong warriors, is overcome. In our nation, then, either we overcome through justice, or we are conquered through injustice.
